content:
STAGE: scope check and design-axis choice
GOAL: Select a hyperbolic SID-table metric that is in-contract and on a different design axis from prefix-ranking (Q_H), bucket count, collision rate, same-bucket ratio.
READ: The task statement only; no SID/recall files are exposed in this session (no read tool, no shell). Evidence for all numbers below is the prompt itself: Q_H(level1)=+0.634, Q_H(level2)=+0.287, Q_H(level3)=+0.393, bucket count=-0.065 on the 97 pairs.
OBSERVED: (a) Any partition-quality score computed on level L mechanically rises to 1 as buckets become singletons, so levels >=2 are near-identifier and unusable as a quality signal; level 1 is the only non-degenerate level, consistent with Q_H peaking at level 1. (b) A raw R^2 of within-bucket dispersion is exploitable by a singleton/identifier table, so it must be compared to a size-matched random-partition baseline (adjusted R^2, K nonempty level-1 codes) to remove the K-dependence. (c) The reference gives two towers (source=query side, target=item side); recall is a source->target retrieval event, so a symmetric average of the two towers is the natural dual-space statistic and uses a constant 1/2 justified by tower symmetry, not tuning.
REASONING: Chosen axis = continuous geometric dispersion / adjusted R^2 of the level-1 partition in the Poincare ball, using an Einstein (Klein) hyperbolic barycentre and squared hyperbolic distances. This is magnitude-sensitive and occupancy-invariant, unlike prefix rank (Q_H) or 0/1 same-bucket indicators. Curvature c=1 fixed (unit ball); scale from training RMS so no tuned constant; mu,sigma from TRAINING items only; no interaction data enters.
EVIDENCE LOCATION: Task prompt, CONTRACT items 1-5 and WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN.
OPEN: None blocking. Risk that level-1-only ignores a genuinely useful deep structure is recorded as the failure mode.

FINAL ANSWER (condensed to fit the 4000-char record limit; full text printed in the response).
METRIC: HYP_ADJ_R2_L1
TITLE: Dual-tower hyperbolic adjusted dispersion R^2 of the level-1 prefix partition.
FORMULA: Items I, N=|I|; level-1 code g(i) in 1..K, K=#nonempty codes; TRAINING subset T. Towers tau in {S(source),T(target)}, frozen reps z_i^tau. mu_tau=mean_T z_i^tau; sigma_tau=RMS_T||z_i^tau-mu_tau||; v_i^tau=(z_i^tau-mu_tau)/sigma_tau; x_i^tau=tanh(||v||)v/||v|| = exp_0(v) in Poincare ball, c=1. d(x,y)=arcosh(1+2||x-y||^2/((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2))). Barycentre beta(B): kappa_j=2x_j/(1+||x_j||^2); gamma_j=1/sqrt(1-||kappa_j||^2); kbar=sum gamma_j kappa_j / sum gamma_j; beta=kbar/(1+sqrt(1-||kbar||^2)). m_tau=beta(all), m_{g,tau}=beta(code g). W_tau=sum_i d(x_i,m_{g(i)})^2; T_tau=sum_i d(x_i,m_tau)^2. HDR_tau=1-(W_tau/(N-K))/(T_tau/(N-1)) if K<N else 0; clip to [-1,1]. METRIC=(HDR_S+HDR_T)/2. Higher better; 0=size-matched random partition; 1=tight codes; negative=anti-coherent.
INPUTS: SID table column 1 only; frozen #126 source+target vectors per item (training-pairs only); TRAINING item ids (for mu,sigma). No recall, no Stage-3, no val/test interaction.
GEOMETRY: c=1 fixed (definition, not tuned). Curvature enters via exp_0=tanh map onto the ball, via the (1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2) boundary blow-up in d, and via the Klein/Einstein gamma_j weights that up-weight boundary points.
WHY IT TRACKS RECALL: recall@10 needs level-1 to be a real behavioural partition in BOTH query (source) and item (target) geometry, so a query can emit a coarse code and still find its top-10 nearby. HDR is the curved, occupancy-corrected fraction of reference dispersion removed by that partition. Adds over Q_H: Q_H is a rank statistic; HDR uses continuous squared hyperbolic distances and sees bucket tightness, is dual-tower (penalises item-only coherence), is invariant to bucket occupancy (not bucket count or same-bucket ratio in disguise), and boundary weighting makes it sensitive to the specific items that decide top-10. Level-1-only by design: R^2 rises to 1 as buckets become singletons, i.e. the known level>=2 identifier collapse.
COMPUTE: O(N*d) with d~512, N=24587, K<=256; a few 1e7 flops, <1s numpy, well under 1 minute; memory O(N*d).
RISKS: reference geometry unrelated to SID space -> noise; tanh saturation/outliers dominate barycentres; (N-K)/(N-1) baseline exact only in Euclidean, approximate in hyperbolic; K near N gives large negative (clipped, K=N -> 0); requires the same frozen reference across all 97 tables.
FAILURE MODE: worst table = level-1 geometrically excellent (high HDR) but level-2/3 codes random/id-sorted inside each bucket; encoder hits the right level-1 code yet must emit arbitrary deep codes, so recall@10 is low while HDR reads high. Structural: metric is blind to levels>=2. Hash/modulo level-1 is correctly strongly negative, hence not a failure.
END METRIC
